segments: 268 and thus came forth:
"That you should reign in his place."
And he, like a wise man, replied:
"Although our father thus commanded,
yet we have a brother who is older than me,
and uncles as well,
who are more suited than me for this.
For moreover, our brother Tolui,
he is the youngest son of the Great Camp (Ordo),
and he was constantly occupied in our father's service,
and he has learned the laws and administrative affairs of the kingdom more than we have.
If it seems good to you,
let him sit upon the throne."
Then they all cried out with one voice:
"It is impossible that the command of our blessed father be broken,
but as he commanded, so let it be!"
And they uncovered their heads,
and cast their sashes over their shoulders,
and Chagatai took his right hand,
and Otchigin his left hand,
and upon a throne of four cushions,
signifying dominion over the four corners of the inhabited world,
they raised him and placed him,
and proclaimed his name 'Khan'.
And Tolui, the youngest brother,
because he had said that the kingdom properly belonged to him,
he was the first of all to give the cup to the Khan to drink,
and he bent on his knees and prostrated before him,
and showed great subjection,
and likewise also the rest of all the brothers who were inside.
And the grandees who were outside the tent-curtain
kneeled to the ground nine times and prostrated themselves before the Khan.
Then they went outside,
and three times prostrated themselves toward the sun according to their custom.
Now when the Khan was established on the throne,
he opened the treasuries and hoards of his father,
and distributed to his brothers, and to his uncles, and to the rest of the grandees,
to each one according to his rank.
And those grandees also chose from among their daughters forty virgins of moon-like {or: luminous? OCR} beauty,
and having adorned them in splendid garments and jewelry strung with precious stones,
they offered them to the Khan.
And all of them rejoiced with very great joy.
Then he enacted a law
that all the laws and regulations enacted by Genghis Khan should be preserved,
and that whoever transgressed against them should die the death.
